'''''Tenuicruris''''' ({{respell|teh|new|ee|KROO|ris}}; {{lit|slender leg}}) is an [[extinct]] genus of [[enantiornithean]] bird known from the [[Early Cretaceous]] ([[Albian]] age) [[Toolebuc Formation]] of Australia. The genus contains a [[Monotypic taxon|single species]], '''''Tenuicruris piscanexum''''', known from a single isolated leg bone. It is the second Mesozoic bird named from Australia.

== Discovery and naming ==
[[File:Richmond, Australia (geological map).jpg|thumb|left|[[Type locality (biology)|Type locality]] (KKF1451 [{{font color|#67D4CF|●}}])]]
The ''Tenuicruris'' fossil material was discovered in outcrops of the [[Toolebuc Formation]] about {{convert|12|km|mi}} northwest of [[Richmond, Queensland|Richmond]] in [[Queensland]], Australia. This site, called 'Dig Site 1', is a public [[fossicking]] area. The specimen is housed in the Kronosaurus Korner Museum, where it is permanently [[Accession number (cultural property)|accessioned]] as specimen KK F1451. It consists of a nearly complete left [[tibiotarsus]].<ref name="Tenuicruris" />

In 2026, Matt A. White and colleagues [[Species description|described]] ''Tenuicruris piscanexum'' as a new genus and species of enantiornithean based on these fossil remains, designating KK F1451 as the [[holotype]] specimen. The [[Genus|generic name]], ''Tenuicruris'', combines the [[Latin]] words {{lang|la|[[:wikt:tenuis#Latin|tenuis]]}}, meaning {{gloss|slender}}, and {{lang|la|[[:wikt:crus#Latin|cruris]]}}, meaning {{gloss|leg}}. The [[Specific name (zoology)|specific name]], ''piscanexum'', is a combination of the Latin {{lang|la|[[:wikt:piscis#Latin|piscis]]}}, meaning {{gloss|fish}}, and {{lang|la|[[:wikt:nexum#Latin|nexum]]}}, meaning {{gloss|binding}}, alluding to the discovery of the holotype within the so-called {{gloss|fish mash}} marker layer identified in Richmond fosskicking sites in.<ref name="Tenuicruris" /> Prior to its description, the only fossil bird named from the Mesozoic of Australia was ''[[Nanantius]]'', which is also known from an isolated tibiotarsus from the Toolebuc Formation.<ref name="Poropat2023" />

== Description and classification ==
[[File:Tenuicruris piscanexum (life restoration by by Travis Tischler).jpg|thumb|[[Life restoration]]]]
The ''T. piscanexum'' holotype tibiotarsus is {{convert|6.54|cm|in}} long. In the coeval ''Nanantius'', this bone is about half the size, at {{cvt|3.14|cm|in}}. When scaled to the same length, this bone is notably more slender in ''Tenuicruris''. ''Tenuicruris'' appears to be distinguishable from all other enantiornitheans by two [[autapomorphies]] (unique derived features): a deep [[Fossa (anatomy)|fossa]] (depression) on the [[Anatomical terms of location#Medial and lateral|lateral]] (outer) surface of the tibiotarsus [[Anatomical terms of location#Proximal and distal|proximal]] to the [[Lateral condyle of tibia|distal condyle]], and distal condyles that are flared when seen from behind.<ref name="Tenuicruris" />

White and colleagues (2026) included ''Tenuicruris'' in a [[phylogenetic]] matrix, but the substantial lack of scorable data for both Australian genera resulted in a large, unresolved [[polytomy]] of most included enantiornitheans. As [[Pengornithidae]] remained well-resolved at the base of Enantiornithes, White et al. regarded ''Tenuricruris'' as an indeterminate, non-pengornithid enantiornithean. They also noted various similarities, such as the presence of a prominent craniolateral [[cnemial crest]], between ''Tenuicruris'' and ''[[Monoenantiornis]]'' and ''[[Qiliania]]'', two Chinese taxa.<ref name="Tenuicruris" />
